subject: Re: Concept Plan MIXED-Provo.pdf
comment: Jonathon: As I understand it, the position advocated by Council member Dave Harding is that the single-family development plan proposed for the Lakeshore Drive property does not comply with the Westside Development Policies, specifically Policy 3.a. which, he believes, requires a mix of housing types. As I will explain below, this position is untenable. The policy in question provides: "3. Encourage Sustainable Residential Development Patterns a. Establish ordinances to require a mix of housing types, lot sizes, and designs to accommodate various stages of life." There is only one requirement of paragraph a, which is to establish ordinances that will, when established, require a mix of housing types. The policy wisely contemplates the Council's careful deliberative process to define mixed housing requirements and to establish them by ordinance. The Council must define parameters and scope for mixed housing types. Those could be to adopt the map created by the committee you and I sat on as the mix of housing types in the southwest quadrant of the city; or on the other extreme to require mixed housing in every single subdivision regardless of size; or something in between. The diﬀerences in opinions of just what the requirements for mixed housing types should be underscores the need for well thought out ordinances. These diﬀerences also emphasize the importance of the Council being cautious and purposeful in it's work. But that work as set forth in the policy has not yet been accomplished. At present no ordinances have been enacted, and there are no requirements, either in ordinance or policy, for a mix of housing types in the Lakeshore Drive development, or in any other development on the southwest side. If the City Council were to deny approval of the proposed single-family development plan of the Lakeshore Drive property on the basis that it does not include a mix of housing types such a denial would be arbitrary and capricious, first because there is no ordinance or policy requiring it, and second because no other development has been held to this non-existent standard. It would be improper to create some sort of de facto ordinance to apply at this moment to this development for no discernible reason. The Council may want to consult the City Attorney prior to contemplating such an action.

subject: RE: Concept Plan MIXED
comment: Hi Jonathan, Thank you for organizing the Zoom calls on the new developments; they're very helpful. I'm hoping my comments below will be constructive, as you present the neighborhood's viewpoints. The city council's role in development is to ensure that the developer's plan aligns with area planning and respects and follows the input of the neighborhood. In this case, the developer's single-family plan aligns with the southwest area map. And we met as a neighborhood, worked with the developer and voted to move forward. However, instead of approving the plan, the city council has inserted themselves in order to advance personal ideals, which they evidently believe should outweigh those of the neighborhood. I have heard the sentiment expressed, over the years, that Provo westside residents routinely receive short shrift from the City. I have not personally felt this way, until now. Feelings aside, the so-called policies that have been cited, in an attempt to bolster Mr. Harding's contention that mixed use must be mandated in this development, cannot be cleanly interpreted, let alone extrapolated, to support his claims. There is an important caveat regarding the neighborhood's acceptance of the developer's plan: The initial single-family development plan that we as a neighborhood agreed upon a couple months ago actually represented a compromise from what we were hoping to see there. Specifically, the single-family 1/4 - 1/3 acre lots were smaller than the 1/2 acre to 1.0 acre RA lots that we would truly love to see, as a continuation of the existing, neighboring lots. So it should be noted that we are already "settling" on the single-family 1/4 to 1/3 acre lots. Lastly, if the city council chooses to mandate mixed use in this development, whereas they have not mandated the same in other west-side residential developments, and whereas the "policies" they cite as justification are nebulous and unenforceable, they may be exposing the City to potential legal liability. Again, I appreciate your help. I'm happy to join in any additional conversations or meetings, as you feel appropriate. Aaron McCullough [redacted-phone]
